You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - NormalDistributionTest.testExtremeValues() constructs a standard NormalDistribution and repeatedly calls cumulativeProbability(-i) and cumulativeProbability(i) for i = 0..99, asserting:
    - For i < 9: the lower tail > 0 and the upper tail < 1.
    - For i ≥ 9: the lower tail < 1e-5 and the upper tail > 0.99999.
    - It also asserts cumulativeProbability(Double.MAX_VALUE) == 1.
  - It explicitly aims to ensure “no convergence exception.”

- Where the exception comes from:
  - NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability(double) computes:
    - dev = x - mean, then returns 0.5 * (1.0 + Erf.erf(dev / (sd * sqrt(2)))) inside a try block that only catches MaxIterationsExceededException (lines 124–138):
      - If MaxIterationsExceededException occurs, it “top-codes” to 0 or 1 when x is more than 20 standard deviations from the mean; otherwise it rethrows.
  - Erf.erf(double) delegates to Gamma.regularizedGammaP(0.5, x*x, 1e-15, 10000) and flips the sign for negative x (lines 50–55).
  - For large |x| (as in the test, e.g., i up to 99; z ≈ i/√2, so z^2 ≈ i^2/2 ≈ 4900), regularizedGammaP(0.5, z^2, …) selects the Q branch (since x ≥ a + 1) and calls Gamma.regularizedGammaQ(a, x, …) (lines 170–174).
  - regularizedGammaQ(a, x, …) evaluates a continued fraction via ContinuedFraction.evaluate(x, epsilon, maxIterations) (lines 252–267).
  - ContinuedFraction.evaluate can overflow intermediate numerator/denominator terms (p2, q2). It attempts limited scaling; if still infinite, it throws a ConvergenceException with CONTINUED_FRACTION_INFINITY_DIVERGENCE (lines 142–181). It can also throw if NaN is encountered (lines 185–189) or if max iterations are exceeded (lines 200–204).

- Why the test fails:
  - For extreme arguments (large i, Double.MAX_VALUE, or infinities), the continued fraction in regularizedGammaQ overflows or becomes unstable and throws ConvergenceException (not MaxIterationsExceededException).
  - NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability only catches MaxIterationsExceededException, so ConvergenceException propagates to the caller, violating the test’s “no convergence exception” expectation.
  - The intended “top-coding” fallback (return 0 or 1 when |x-mean| > 20*sd) is only triggered for MaxIterationsExceededException; it is not applied when ConvergenceException occurs.
  - Consequently:
    - For large finite i (e.g., i ≥ 9 in the loop), a ConvergenceException can be thrown instead of returning a value close to 0 or 1.
    - For Double.MAX_VALUE (or +/-Infinity), Erf.erf attempts gamma computations with huge/infinite x and also throws ConvergenceException, so the final assertEquals(…, 1) cannot even execute.

- Root cause:
  - Inadequate exception handling and tail-guarding in NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability:
    - It relies on Erf.erf for all inputs and only catches MaxIterationsExceededException, but Erf.erf can and does throw ConvergenceException for extreme inputs due to overflow in the continued fraction evaluation.
    - Top-coding logic is bound to a specific exception type instead of being applied for all computation failures or preemptively for extreme tails (including infinities).

- Impacted code snippets:
  - NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability(double) (lines 124–138): only catches MaxIterationsExceededException and applies tail top-coding in that catch.
  - Erf.erf(double) (lines 50–55): implemented via Gamma.regularizedGammaP with epsilon 1e-15 and maxIterations 10000, which eventually uses a continued fraction for large arguments.
  - ContinuedFraction.evaluate(...) (lines 126–207): throws ConvergenceException when overflow persists or NaN occurs.

- Conclusion:
  - The failure stems from unhandled ConvergenceException thrown deep in erf/gamma for extreme inputs. NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability must either:
    - Preemptively handle extreme tails (including +/-Infinity) and return 0 or 1 without calling Erf.erf; or
    - Broaden its catch to include ConvergenceException (or MathException) and apply the same top-coding logic as currently used for MaxIterationsExceededException.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
